svg.title: Conditional sparse-verdict errors with explicit denominators and different vertical scales
svg.desc: False-unstable errors are divided by96 reference-stable graph-scale evaluations per method and draw budget. False-stable errors are divided by84 reference-unstable evaluations. At110 draws the false-unstable counts are63of96 for effective resistance and57of96 for uniform. The only false-stable observation is1of84 for effective resistance at20draws; every other method-budget false-stable count is0of84. Left vertical scale is0to100percent and right scale0to1.5percent. Zero observed misses is not a bound on population risk. Evaluations reuse18 underlying samples across10 scales.

g.text: Different y-axis scales: 0–100% at left; 0–1.5% at right. Numerators count sparse-verdict errors.
Each method/budget: 96 reference-stable and 84 reference-unstable graph-scale evaluations; samples are reused across scales.
